accepted_phrases: Auditory masking means that one sound can affect perception of another and that a target sound has a higher masked threshold in the presence of a particular masking noise. The reference measures neither this bus nor any shortlisted earbud. Therefore one casual bus comparison in which no obvious difference was heard cannot establish that two earbuds are equivalent in a quiet room, on a controlled bus comparison, or for another listener. Treat the bus result as confounded by masking and by unknown content, listening level, fit, tips, source, settings, and codec configuration rather than as proof of a universal price boundary.

An audio codec encodes or decodes an audio stream, and software codecs compress and decompress digital audio to reduce storage or transmission bandwidth while retaining quality. The frozen Avantree page supplies only a seller aptX CD-like-quality claim inside a Windows USB-adapter and earbud bundle; it supplies no controlled result for the buyer's actual source, operating system, active codec, settings, content, level, or listening conditions. Meaningful codec comparisons commonly use double-blind methods and similar or identical bitrates. In an ABX comparison, A and B are known, X is randomized as one of them, and reliable identification over predetermined trials is required before claiming a perceptible difference under those circumstances. Thus the aptX label can affect value only after the actual playback configuration is verified and a matched, preferably blinded and repeatable comparison shows a buyer-relevant benefit; it cannot establish a universal tier premium or an automatic sound-quality winner.

At the frozen snapshot, YOVDA K98 displays SKU B097D3SK5S, $29.99, and no review score and makes seller claims about gaming latency, game and music modes, and play time. Generic F9 TWS displays SKU B09S3NMKZT, $43.28, and no review score and says its case doubles as a power bank and phone holder. Avantree DG45 plus TWS120 displays SKU B08T1KT57M, $59.99, and no review score; it combines a Windows USB Bluetooth adapter with true-wireless earbuds, states a restricted compatibility scope, and makes aptX and battery claims. KW-01 displays SKU B09MVK5ND6, $139.90, and no review score and makes game-mode, driver, noise-reduction, and play-time claims. These are frozen seller observations, none contains an independent matched sound-quality comparison, no-review displays are not zero-star efficacy results, and the bundle price is not a like-for-like earbud price. The fresh ladder ends at $139.90 and contains no eligible $200-to-$300 offer, so it cannot cover the requested $30-to-$300 range or establish a universal cutoff or exact winner.

Before testing, verify current checkout, exact model, seller, a bounded return window, warranty, complete bundle contents, the exact playback device and operating system, and the available and active codec or mode. Require at least two distinct returnable price tiers and predeclare maximum spend plus minimum fit, connection, call, battery, control, and latency requirements. Compare the same excerpts and volume-matched content in randomized or blinded order first in quiet and then on the ordinary bus, keeping fit, tips, source, settings, equalization, and codec condition fixed except for the variable being tested. For codec value, compare like with like at similar or identical bitrate where applicable and repeat predetermined trials to check reliable identification. Record detectable difference and preference separately. Return failures and choose the cheapest eligible tested tier that passes the predeclared requirements, or buy none if fewer than two tiers remain or no tier passes. This trial may identify a conditional threshold for this buyer among the tested tiers, but it cannot establish a universal $30-to-$300 cutoff while the $200-to-$300 tier remains uncaptured.

The frozen evidence supports neither a universal diminishing-returns cutoff nor an immediate exact-product winner. The four seller pages span $29.99 to $139.90, all show no review score, mix different feature and bundle scopes, and contain no matched sound-quality comparison. Because no fresh eligible $200-to-$300 true-wireless offer was captured, the material cannot locate a boundary near the friend's reported $280 price. The casual bus result is confounded by auditory masking and uncontrolled listening conditions. The Avantree aptX wording also cannot move the value boundary by itself; codec value must be shown on the actual configuration through a matched, preferably blinded and repeatable comparison. Defer the universal cutoff and direct winner, run the bounded returnable cross-tier trial, and choose the cheapest tested tier that satisfies the predeclared requirements or buy none. Report any result only as this buyer's conditional threshold among tested tiers, not as a universal market cutoff.

Do not select YOVDA, F9, Avantree, or KW-01 from frozen price, seller features, a no-review display, bundle value, or a codec logo alone. Defer the universal cutoff, verify exact checkout and playback conditions, compare at least two returnable tiers under the matched quiet-and-bus protocol, and choose the cheapest tested tier that passes the predeclared requirements or buy none.
The evidence supports no universal $30-to-$300 cutoff or immediate exact-product winner; use the terminating matched returnable tier trial and keep its result buyer-specific.

research_subgoals.description: Build the exact four-row frozen offer matrix, preserving SKU, price, no-review display, seller-feature, bundle, compatibility, and independent-test scope, and identify the uncaptured $200-to-$300 tier.

Determine whether the Avantree aptX claim should affect value by separating a codec's function, the seller's bundle claim, ABX detection, matched bitrate, and double-blind method from an actual result on the buyer's configuration.
Explain why auditory masking and uncontrolled conditions prevent the casual bus comparison from proving quiet-room equivalence or a universal price boundary.

Specify a terminating returnable cross-tier trial that verifies eligibility, fixes listening variables, tests codec value appropriately, records detection separately from preference, and yields the cheapest passing tested tier or no purchase.
Reject unsupported price, seller-feature, bundle, no-review, bus-anecdote, and codec shortcuts, then state the evidence-bounded decision and the scope of any trial-derived threshold.

query_requirements.text: Build the exact frozen YOVDA K98, generic F9 TWS, Avantree DG45 plus TWS120, and KW-01 comparison matrix with SKU, price, no-review display, seller features, bundle and compatibility scope, and absence of independent comparison; state exactly where the fresh price ladder ends and which requested tier is uncaptured.

Assess whether the Avantree aptX claim should change the value boundary by verifying the actual playback configuration and applying codec-function, ABX, double-blind, and similar-or-identical-bitrate scope without treating a general method as a product result.
Explain what auditory masking does and does not establish, and why one uncontrolled bus comparison cannot prove quiet-room equivalence, a shortlist ranking, or a universal diminishing-returns cutoff.

Give an operational matched returnable cross-tier trial with exact eligibility gates, fixed source and listening variables, quiet and ordinary-bus conditions, randomized or blinded comparison, codec-specific controls, detection-versus-preference records, and a terminal cheapest-passing-tier or buy-none rule.

State whether any universal $30-to-$300 cutoff or immediate exact-product winner is supported, reject every unsupported shortcut, and distinguish a buyer-specific threshold among tested tiers from a universal market conclusion.
